lyrics:
[Intro: chiming clean guitar, soft bass]

[Verse 1: earnest male tenor]
I yelled about the milk you spilled
I missed the play, I worked too late
I thought that fathers had to be
A wall, a wallet and a weight

[Pre-Chorus: drums enter]
You were so small, and I was scared
And I called it being strict

[Chorus: full band, open and loud]
I was new at this
You were my first try
I learned it all on you
And I'm sorry for the times I got it wrong
I was twenty-four, I was new at this
You turned out good in spite of me
You are why I got better at it

[Verse 2: voice softer, guitar and piano]
Your sister got the dad who knew
To kneel down, and to count to ten
You got the one still figuring out
The difference between boys and men

[Pre-Chorus: drums building]
I can't go back and take the fear
Out of your father's voice

[Chorus: full band, open and loud]
I was new at this
You were my first try
I learned it all on you
And I'm sorry for the times I got it wrong
I was twenty-four, I was new at this
You turned out good in spite of me
You are why I got better at it

[Guitar Solo: short, melodic]

[Bridge: band drops to guitar and voice]
Now you've got one of your own
And I can see you being kind
If any of that came from me
It's the best thing I'll leave behind

[Final Chorus: full band, harmonies]
I was new at this
You were my first try
I learned it all on you
And I'm sorry for the times I got it wrong
I was twenty-four, I was new at this
You turned out good in spite of me
You are why I got better at it

[Outro: guitar chiming, "It's okay, Dad." "I know. I'm still sorry."]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 83 BPM, 4/4, E major. Mid-slow, earnest and open-hearted.

VOICE: Male tenor, clear and sincere with a slight grain, quiet in the verses and full-voiced in the choruses, with a harmony above in the last one. Two spoken lines at the end, son then father.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean, chiming electric guitar arpeggio, a second overdriven guitar in the choruses, bass, a steady rock drum kit, piano, a string pad, a short melodic guitar solo.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro guitar. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:38 Pre-chorus. 0:48 Chorus 1. 1:22 Verse 2. 1:48 Pre-chorus. 1:58 Chorus 2. 2:32 Guitar solo. 2:46 Bridge. 3:06 Final chorus. 3:38 Outro, two spoken lines, ends 3:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s radio rock ballad: polished, bright and wide, guitars layered, vocal clean and loud.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Your sister got the dad who knew to kneel down, and to count to ten' at 1:28.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original apologises to a girlfriend. The apology men of that generation find hardest, and most owe, is to the first child they practised on.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Ashamed, explaining, proud of him, forgiven.
